params.place: on the map: the North Atlantic, Greenland beside Canada

moments.what: Greenland's outline draws itself and its name writes on
Canada's coast lights up beside it, a short gap of sea between
Europe lights up far off to the east
a long red line shoots from Greenland across the ocean
the camera pulls back as the line lands on Denmark, a pin drops on Copenhagen
a big question mark stamps over Greenland

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Greenland sits next to Canada, not Europe, yet it belongs to Denmark. Why?

params.place: on the map: Greenland, Denmark lifted onto it

moments.what: Greenland paints in white from the south
the island rises off the map with a shadow
a ruler draws along its length
a sign BIGGEST ISLAND stamps onto the ice
Denmark's shape lifts off Europe
it slides across the ocean onto Greenland at true scale
Denmark's shape settles onto the ice with a bump, its name writing on
Denmark sits tiny in one corner, a pulse round it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And it's no small corner: Greenland is the biggest island on Earth. Lay Denmark on top of it, and Denmark covers just one sliver.

params.place: on the map: Greenland, the ice sheet

moments.what: green grass sprouts along the coast
the camera dips toward the green coast
the grass flickers and fades
the grass withers to brown
the camera glides over the inland
white ice spreads from the middle outwards
the ice covers almost all of it, a thermometer sign with the share
snow drifts across the map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Stranger still, most of it isn't green at all: 81% of the island lies under one giant sheet of ice.

params.place: on the map: Iceland to Greenland's south-west coast

moments.what: the map goes old and sepia, the name GREENLAND rubs out
a year dial spins back
a Viking longship appears off Iceland, a red-bearded sailor at the bow
its striped sail fills
it sails west from Iceland
it lands on the south-west coast and the name GREENLAND paints back on
small farm huts pop up along the fjords

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So who named it Greenland? Over a thousand years ago, Erik the Red, a Viking sailing from Iceland, picked the name, supposedly to tempt settlers.

params.place: on the map: Denmark-Norway to Greenland's west coast

moments.what: the farm huts stand on the coast
they fade one by one, snow covers them
Denmark glows across the sea
a ship with a cross on its sail leaves Bergen
a man in a black coat stands on its deck
the camera pulls back as it crosses the ocean
Denmark and Norway fill one shared red
a red-and-white flag plants on the west coast

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: His farms died out. So how did Denmark get it? A missionary, Hans Egede, sailed from Denmark-Norway, then one kingdom, and started a colony.

params.place: on the map: Scandinavia and the North Atlantic islands

moments.what: the camera swings to Scandinavia
a cannon smoke puff and a cracked shield over Denmark
Norway's red cracks off Denmark
Norway slides into Sweden's blue
a treaty scroll unrolls over the sea, the camera pulls back
a ribbon ties Greenland to Denmark
a ribbon ties Iceland
a ribbon ties the Faroe Islands
all three glow red with Denmark

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here's the twist. After backing Napoleon and losing, that kingdom had to hand Norway to Sweden, but the treaty left Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands with Denmark.

params.place: on the map: Iceland, then Nuuk on Greenland's west coast

moments.what: Iceland glows
its ribbon snaps and it turns its own blue
Iceland lifts off the map, free
the camera glides to Greenland
its ribbon holds
the year board starts to rise on the coast
the year lands on the board with a stamp
the camera starts to close on Nuuk
a small parliament house rises at Nuuk
Nuuk's name writes on, a red-and-white flag waves
a gold star lands on Nuuk

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Iceland broke away long ago. Greenland stayed, and in 1979 it won home rule, with its own parliament in Nuuk, its capital.

params.place: on the map: Greenland whole, a ballot box at Nuuk

moments.what: a second year board stamps beside the first
a ballot box appears at Nuuk
a key hangs over the box
ballots drop into the box
the camera pulls back over the whole island
the ribbon to Denmark stretches thin
Denmark flashes red at the far end of the ribbon
the ribbon starts to fray and shake
the population sign rises and its figure counts up
the figure lands, tiny figures dot the coast
a pair of scissors hovers over the ribbon

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then in 2009 came self-rule, and with it the right to choose independence by its own vote. So the biggest island on Earth stays with Denmark until its 56,945 people decide otherwise.

params.place: on the map: the two islands, then the hook's North Atlantic

moments.what: a pin glows on Iceland
a pin glows on the Faroes
a question mark hops between them
both islands rise off the map
a comment bubble pops up
its words write on: ICELAND OR FAROES?
the camera pulls back to the North Atlantic
Greenland's outline fades to the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Iceland or the Faroes: which island should we explain next? Tell me in the comments. And look again at that map:
